Experiments show that CiFormer reduces mean absolute error and improves top-1 beam-pair selection accuracy by 3.15 percentage points over the strongest baseline. Visualizations and ablation studies support dual-endpoint sensing and selective cross-view interaction in capturing propagation-relevant dependencies, suggesting broader applications in wireless tasks beyond beam prediction.
item.dc:creator: Shiliang Lu, Lu Bai, Ziwei Huang, Xiang Cheng

item.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting: Continual Learning for Radar Waveform Classification
item.description: arXiv:2610.18404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated radar waveform recognition classifies the waveform and modulation type of a received signal. As new waveform variants appear over time, a deployed classifier must learn them without retraining from scratch. Catastrophic Forgetting occurs when learning new waveforms overwrites prior knowledge. Continual Learning (CL) methods tackle this challenge, but prior radar studies only evaluate a few methods on narrow benchmarks. Practitioners lack evidence on which method to deploy or which mechanisms are effective. This work presents the first large-scale benchmark of continual learning for radar waveform recognition. Eighteen CL methods are evaluated on a sequential ten-task problem, drawn from four public datasets spanning 54 waveforms, under task- and class-incremental (TIL, CIL) settings and single- and multi-epoch regimes. Methods that retain data from old tasks lead both TIL and CIL settings. Plain replay alone closes 77-88% of the gap between the lower and upper practical limits under TIL, but only 46-55% under CIL. The internal mechanisms of the leading methods are ablated and statistically tested to identify effective mechanisms. Each ablation is paired against its full method over n=6 training seeds, topped up to n=12 when inconclusive, and p-values are Holm-Bonferroni corrected within each method's family. Ablation results show that several mechanisms confer smaller but statistically significant gains. Combining these mechanisms improves the leading F1 score by 3.4-5.5% and 2.7-4.9% under TIL and CIL, respectively, and the combined models exceed every benchmarked method in both settings for all SNRs. These results give researchers of radar waveform classification systems a mechanism-level basis for design.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Rabie, Chinthana J. Panagamuwa, Konstantinos G. Kyriakopoulos

item.title: A Three-Axis Rydberg Atomic Receiver Model for Polarization-Based Direction-of-Arrival Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.18450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a three-axis Rydberg atomic receiver model for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation of the radio frequency (RF) signal source. Three nominally orthogonal RF local oscillators (LOs), each assigned a distinct frequency offset, project the weak incident RF field into resolvable complex beat coefficients in the optical readout. A beat-vector observation is obtained by adopting a response calibration mechanism that maps the coefficients onto the three axes of the Cartesian coordinate system. For a known circularly polarised RF signal, this observation induces a direction-dependent Rydberg steering vector, enabling maximum-likelihood DoA estimation. The pro posed procedure translates the Rydberg beat-vector front end into a highly sensitive RF field DoA sensor. Simulation results show that trace-level beat extraction supports the proposed DoA sensing workflow and provides a basis for comparison with a traditional vector antenna (VA) benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Bangyan Xia, Bo Tan

item.title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults
item.description: arXiv:2610.18494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective digital measures of depression severity could complement conventional symptom assessments and facilitate more timely clinical evaluation. Here, we investigated whether task-evoked eye movements provide interpretable behavioral markers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 155 participants aged 14--20 years completed emotional-spatial free-viewing and memory-guided recall tasks and were stratified by 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. We examined 19 prespecified eye-movement features across six task-informed domains using covariate-adjusted ordinal-trend models. Greater depression severity was associated with lower gaze-allocation entropy (standardized $\beta=-0.599$), fewer inter-area switches ($\beta=-0.526$), longer first target-entry latency ($\beta=0.572$), and lower target dwell proportion ($\beta=-0.678$; all false-discovery-rate-adjusted $q<0.001$). Emotion-specific attentional-bias measures were not associated with severity, whereas associations involving fixation dispersion weakened after adjustment for anxiety symptoms. In a complementary machine-learning analysis incorporating 44 candidate eye-movement features and demographic covariates, a three-stage cascade classifier achieved the highest four-class stratification performance (accuracy, 0.665; macro-F1, 0.670; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.869), outperforming single-stage and two-stage approaches. Together, these findings identify altered visual exploration and memory-guided gaze control as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity, rather than generalized negative attentional bias. These results support further prospective evaluation of task-evoked eye tracking as a complementary approach for timely severity assessment and clinical decision support.
item.dc:creator: Youxiang Sun, Yujie Nie, Zhuoru Wu, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Xiang Li, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

item.title: Contactless gait-derived features as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents
item.description: arXiv:2610.18510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timely assessment of depression severity in adolescents is essential for guiding clinical care, yet conventional evaluations rely on episodic clinical assessments and symptom rating scales. Contactless gait analysis offers a potentially scalable approach to capturing objective behavioral features associated with depression. Here, we introduce the Long-Distance 3D Adolescent Depression Gait Dataset (LD3D-ADG), comprising depth-sensor gait recordings from 119 adolescents at a single center, including 39 healthy controls, 41 with mild depression, and 39 with moderate-to-severe depression. We developed UMLPA-GCN, a graph convolutional network that models spatiotemporal gait dynamics across three anatomically defined skeletal partitions. In participant-independent five-fold cross-validation, UMLPA-GCN achieved 75.63% classification accuracy, a macro-F1 score of 75.52%, and a macro-area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.839 (95% confidence interval, 0.779--0.899). Class-specific recall was 87.18%, 63.41%, and 76.92% for healthy controls, mild depression, and moderate-to-severe depression, respectively. At the participant level, reduced arm swing, slower pelvic movement, restricted joint range of motion, and greater arm-swing asymmetry were identified as leading potential digital biomarkers contributing to depression severity assessment, associated with higher 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for contactless digital depression severity stratification in adolescents. Further external and prospective validation is needed to establish their utility for longitudinal monitoring and timely clinical assessment.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Liu, Xiang Li, Guangxin Dai, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Hanchi Liu, Jiahui Niu, Yujie Nie, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

item.title: RetinaSC: Retinal Semantic Communication Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.18824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a lightweight semantic com- munication framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from fundus images pertaining specifically to the APTOS2019 dataset. The framework includes semantic encoder designed using ResNet34, U-Net, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures. Further, the trained models are used to train the same framework for IDRiD dataset using transfer learning approach. Such a framework will enable the telemedicine sector in the early detection of DR and prevent total blindness. The results reveal that for APTOS, task-oriented semantic systems can achieve satisfactory robust performance (more than 0.8 weighted F1 score for ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B0) across different channels. In particular, considering the trade-off between complexity, latency, throughput, and F1 score, MobileNetV2 is the best model with weighted F1 score of 0.76-0.78 for both task and reconstruction- oriented modules and end-to-end latency of only 8.162 ms.
item.dc:creator: Avani Shinod, Rangineni Rushitha, Asqeem Nas, Anirban Bhowal, Shikha Baghel

item.title: Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning for Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation: From Physical Alignment to Scene Aggregation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied Audio-Visual Navigation (AVN) requires an agent to locate sound targets by jointly leveraging visual and auditory cues. While prior work has achieved notable success with static sound sources, real-world scenarios often involve moving targets, giving rise to the more challenging problem of \textbf{Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation (D-AVN)}. Existing approaches largely rely on semantic auditory features, which limits generalization to unheard sound categories and hinders fine-grained spatial reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel \textbf{Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning} framework for D-AVN. In the Physical Alignment stage, the proposed \textbf{Intensity-Calibrated Geometry Encoder (ICGE)} performs physics-informed alignment of sound intensity with visual geometry to capture category-agnostic spatial correspondence. In the Scene Aggregation stage, a Transformer-based \textbf{Cross-Modal Scene Aggregator (CMSA)} dynamically integrates multi-modal features to construct a robust state representation for policy learning. Extensive experiments on Replica and Matterport3D demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art success rates, while significantly improving generalization and navigation efficiency in complex environments and under unheard sound scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Jia Li, Yinfeng Yu

item.title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins
item.description: arXiv:2610.14187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Urban traffic systems are becoming increasingly complex, demanding real-time traffic perception, proactive collision prediction, and intelligent management to improve safety and reduce congestion. Although AI-driven traffic management has shown strong promise, its success relies on diverse, high-quality data spanning critical scenarios such as collisions, near-collisions, and traffic rule violations. Digital twins offer a powerful solution by enabling synchronized virtual replicas of physical traffic environments for real-time monitoring, collision prediction, traffic-flow optimization, and diverse realistic scenario generation. However, continuously synchronizing a high-fidelity urban traffic digital twin through edge surveillance cameras requires substantial edge-cloud communication, and transmitting raw video streams leads to severe bandwidth and latency constraints. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a semantic communication-based edge-cloud framework for real-time urban traffic digital twin applications. By leveraging edge intelligence to extract and transmit only task-relevant semantic traffic information instead of full video feeds, the proposed framework significantly reduces communication overhead while preserving the essential dynamics needed for accurate real-time digital twin reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate more than 99% transmission savings and an average trajectory reconstruction error of only 0.12 m, confirming the proposed framework as an effective, scalable, and low-latency solution for AI-enabled urban traffic digital twin applications.
item.dc:creator: Murat Arda Onsu, Arman Dogru, Poonam Lohan, Burak Kantarci, Aisha Syed

item.title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
item.description: arXiv:2610.14208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Kataria, Davin Sequeira, Arti Yardi

item.title: Global Optimality of Pose Graph Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.14655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pose Graph Optimization (PGO) is a classical and widely applied problem in state estimation for robotics, playing a fundamental role in localization, mapping, and navigation. Yet, it is nonconvex in nature and may have many local minimizers, thus difficult to analyze. In this paper, we investigate the optimization landscape and establish a sufficient condition of global optimality for PGO. The ultimate goal of this paper is to theoretically confirm that the optimization landscape is benign and attractive around the global minimizer, if noise is smaller than an explicit and a priori bound. To reveal such an insight, this paper develops three main technical results. First, we identify a proper basin of attraction (BOA) containing global minimizer, and characterize its geometric property by showing that its radius is controlled by noise in an explicit way. Then, by exploring the first order optimality conditions of PGO, we prove that a local minimizer is globally optimal if a noise-controlled criterion is satisfied. Finally, by combining above two results, we prove that one and only one local minimizer exists in the BOA and this minimizer is globally optimal, when the noise is smaller than an explicit bound that can be verified a priori. Numerical simulations validate the proposed theory under various random cases, showing that the obtained conditions provide an effective criterion for certifying the global optimality of PGO.
item.dc:creator: Shuan Ding, Ruishuang Chen, Mengfan Cao, Zaiyue Yang

item.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Thermal Human Perception from Dataset to Deployment
item.description: arXiv:2610.14846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Indoor human perception is the foundation for smart homes and healthcare. However, RGB cameras raise privacy concerns in private indoor environments, while low-resolution thermal cameras provide limited spatial and semantic information. Large-scale indoor thermal datasets and real-world deployments remain limited. Here, we introduce Indoor RGB-T, a large-scale paired RGB--thermal dataset for indoor human perception. The dataset covers 20 indoor rooms and contains 90,576 80x62 thermal frames, 87,016 temporally matched RGB--thermal pairs, and 115,557 annotated human bounding boxes. We establish benchmarks for robust thermal occupant-state detection with 0.75 mAP and occupancy estimation with an accuracy of 0.847 in unseen rooms. We further evaluate RGB-to-thermal and thermal-to-RGB translation, achieving a temperature MAE of 0.654 C and an R2 of 0.923. Finally, we deploy the thermal perception model on a commercial sleep-monitoring system in the real world. Field testing with 100 participants and deployment of approximately 1,000 devices further demonstrate its practical feasibility. We identify practical challenges that motivate future research directions, including environmental thermal interference, sensing range and multi-person occlusion. The code, trained models and partial dataset are available at https://github.com/kailaisun/RGBT and https://huggingface.co/skl24/RGBT.
item.dc:creator: Kailai Sun, Yue Cui, Xinwei Wang, Zijie Gao, Baoshen Guo, Zhiqing Hong, Irfan Qaisar, Xu Yang, Yueting Li, Dian Fan, Qianchuan Zhao

item.title: Harnessing SPAD Noise: Test-Time Gated Attention for Indoor Depth Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to hardware-dependent 3D sensing modalities, yet predicting precise metric depth remains a persistent challenge due to intrinsic scale ambiguity, edge bleeding, and limited zero-shot generalization in unseen environments. Recent multi-modal approaches incorporate 1D/3D Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) data to resolve these ambiguities, but they mainly treat SPAD noise as a harmful artifact required for denoising or leave the noise ignored. In this paper, we present an essentially different insight: native SPAD noise is an informative prior that implicitly encodes deterministic environmental characteristics. Driven by this paradigm shift, we introduce a novel, lightweight Test-Time Gated Attention framework by Harnessing SPAD Noise, therefore dubbed HSN. Tailored for indoor scenarios, HSN leverages the synergistic combination of 1D SPAD histograms and Gate Adapters (GAs). Through three complementary optimization phases, it generates channel-wise gated attention vectors to dynamically adjust encoder feature maps at inference time, effectively resolving ambiguous scale and boundary challenges without the heavy computational overhead or dense 3D modalities that other TTA methods suffer from. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world indoor benchmarks show that HSN achieves state-of-the-art metric depth accuracy in in-domain settings, while exhibiting even greater potential under zero-shot generalization to unfamiliar environments. Furthermore, interpretability analysis reveals that the proposed gated attention mechanism adaptively shifts attention toward deeper semantic layers under intensifying SPAD noise. Code will be made publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Yiquan Gao

item.title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.15490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.
item.dc:creator: Jiajia Guo, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin, Jun Zhang

item.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN
item.description: arXiv:2610.15995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents AutoSec-RAN, a specification-grounded large language model (LLM) framework for automated security triage of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testing. Unlike approaches relying on static rule sets or privileged access to raw packet captures, AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct through two Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) stages over a curated corpus of 69 O-RAN, 3GPP, and adjacent standards documents, then selectively augments inference with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the same specification index. At inference, the model receives only an investigator-style question and a scenario metadata block, simulating an automated analyst operating without raw packet evidence. AutoSec-RAN is validated on a purpose-built 5G/O-RAN testbed across labeled fronthaul distributed denial of service replay scenarios. A Gemma-4-31B judge LLM scores each candidate's answer on faithfulness, correctness, and actionability relative to a reference authored from full packet capture and log evidence. AutoSec-RAN achieves a mean judge overall score of 0.713 across all 313 evaluation items (0.755 restricted to the five supervised taxonomy classes), clearing the 0.70 reporting threshold, and a blended score of 0.778 (0.808 supervised-only) when cosine similarity over Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI) General Embedding (BGE) is incorporated as a secondary semantic signal. The framework performs strongest on mitigation and threat-model reasoning (with a mean overall of 0.849 and 0.848, respectively) and identifies a measurable gap on the held-out attack-direction class (0.515), a controlled result that exposes a specific training data requirement. These results establish specification-grounded LoRA fine-tuning combined with RAG retrieval as a viable foundation for automated security validation of AI-native O-RAN.
item.dc:creator: Anoop Mishra, Joshua Moore, Aly Sabri Abdalla, Vuk Marojevic

item.title: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.16020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Layer-wise post-training quantization methods let each layer compensate for the quantization error inherited from earlier layers. We ask under what assumptions such compensation guarantees a network output error no larger than without it. For linear networks of any depth, with the required calibration Gram matrices invertible, if the rounding error of each layer has zero conditional mean and a deterministic second-moment map common to both schemes, as under subtractive dither on an unbounded grid, then compensation with strengths in $[0,1]$ fixed in advance gives a mean-square output error no larger than no compensation, each scheme being followed along its own trajectory. The exact gain separates error removed directly from reduced excitation of later rounding noise. Outside this setting the comparison can fail. With rectified linear activations it fails for two independent reasons: noise changes activation states, and, even when no state changes, the correction moves error from samples on which a unit is inactive to samples on which it is active. With stable activations, commutators between the calibration projection and the activation patterns bound the excess. With a bounded codebook, even unique exact layer-wise minimizers with no overload can give a larger output error. For fixed rounding errors it already fails for two scalar linear layers, refuting a published universal guarantee. An exact residual identity gives the necessary and sufficient condition on a common layer input. All these comparisons hold the calibration input fixed. On two 8B models at 4 bits, fixed half-strength compensation beat uncompensated rounding in every model, text and draw tested, yet no rule for choosing the strength beat a layer-wise rule consistently, and lowering the full-network loss on the data used to choose did not reliably lower it on new text.
item.dc:creator: Tianhao Guo

item.title: Delay-Doppler Duality: Simplifying Exact Equalization of Zak-OTFS in Time or in Frequency
item.description: arXiv:2610.16033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Zak-OTFS carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, and given the input-output (I/O) relation at one DD point in a frame, we can predict the I/O relation at all other points. While it is simple to acquire the effective wireless channel with Zak-OTFS, the cost of embracing inter-carrier interference is equalization complexity. The cost of linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) equalization grows cubically with the frame size. We describe how to use channel knowledge to reduce equalization complexity. For any pulse shaping filter, and for fractional delays and Dopplers, we show that the DD channel matrix is unitarily similar, through the discrete Zak transform, to a time-domain (TD) matrix that is a weighted sum of cyclic delay and Doppler operators, where the weights are the taps of the effective channel. We also obtain a dual frequency-domain (FD) form through an additional Fourier transform. The TD matrix is banded with a width set by the delay spread that is independent of the Doppler spread, whereas the FD matrix is banded with a width set only by the Doppler spread. We design a receiver that reads off the two widths from the channel estimate, selects the cheaper domain, and solves the banded system exactly, using a bordered Cholesky factorization that treats the quasi-periodic wrap-around without sacrificing degrees of freedom. Filters that decay slowly need a few preconditioned conjugate gradient steps. We show that the complexity of equalization becomes linear in the frame size. Simulations match direct DD-LMMSE error rates with three to four orders of magnitude fewer multiplications. A single receiver handles channels with very different delay and Doppler characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Mudasir Ahmad Sheikh, Robert Calderbank

item.title: Robust Quickest Change Detection with Cost-Efficient Experiment Design and Unknown Post-Change Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quickest change detection problem is studied where the decision-maker has access to multiple experiments, but can choose only one experiment at a time to detect the change. The true post-change distribution under each experiment is unknown, but known to belong to a family of distributions. It is assumed that each of these families of distributions has an element that is least favorable in a well-defined sense. An algorithm is proposed that is designed using the least favorable distributions. It is shown that the algorithm is first-order asymptotically optimal, as the rate of false alarms goes to zero. This algorithm minimizes the worst-case average detection delay over all post-change distributions within the assumed families, subject to a constraint on the average run length to false alarm and constraints on the average fraction of time each experiment is performed before change.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Vincent Lubenia, Taposh Banerjee

item.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
item.description: arXiv:2610.16707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xinjie, Dier Tang, Shaolun-Huang

item.title: Making Tensor Decoupling More Robust and Less Parametric
item.description: arXiv:2610.16937v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensor decoupling algorithms recover compact representations of multivariate functions by combining linear factor matrices with univariate internal nonlinearities. We identify two limitations of recent methods. First, their performance is not invariant to mismatched output or gradient magnitudes, and second, their spline internals require manual tuning of their degrees of freedom. We propose two lightweight fixes. The first is a preprocessing step that rescales the input Jacobian tensor, removing both the bias towards larger magnitude outputs and the ill-conditioning of certain factor updates caused by such a mismatch. The second replaces B-spline internals by penalized splines coupled with generalized cross-validation, making the method less dependent on the user selecting the right number of control points. Finally, we release an efficient open-source JAX implementation of our algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Rochkoulets, Joppe De Jonghe, Mariya Ishteva

item.title: On the Multi-Weight Shift-Sum Iterative Decoding of Short BCH Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates a shift-sum decoding algorithm that employs dual codewords. Existing dual codeword shift-sum decoding schemes mainly rely on minimum-weight dual codewords. However, the number of such codewords is often limited, which restricts the amount of reliability information available to the decoder. To address this issue, we extend the component counting mechanism from minimum-weight dual codewords to dual codewords whose Hamming weights lie within a prescribed upper bound. We further introduce a normalized component counting rule to suppress the overcounting bias caused by the much larger populations of higher-weight classes. Based on this framework, we develop a hard-decision iterative error reduction decoder and a soft information-aided iterative error reduction decoder. Numerical results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing minimum-weight shift-sum baselines especially for short codes where additional dual codeword information is particularly valuable.
item.dc:creator: Yinglei Yang, Di Zhang, Aimin Li, Yifei Shen, Alexey Frolov, Bo Gu

item.title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
item.description: arXiv:2610.17154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. For moving digits, one shared spiking encoder fed two readouts, one reconstructing the image and one decoding the digit's position. Compute energy was estimated from counted synaptic operations. The SNN decoded what and where at once. It reconstructed the stimuli with a structural similarity (SSIM) of up to 0.93, refining the reconstruction as spikes accumulated, and tracked a randomly moving target with a mean error of 1.33 pixels on a $32\times32$ grid. Its fidelity nearly matched that of the best of 17 larger spiking and artificial decoders (5.9 million to 1.7 billion parameters, versus 5.4 million), and at a mean firing rate of 14.2% it needed an estimated $\sim$70-fold less compute energy than a dense artificial network of the same architecture. Dynamic visual scenes can thus be decoded from retinal population activity in the spike domain, with a compact network and at a compute cost compatible with implantable and wearable neural interfaces, supporting spike-native decoders for visual prostheses.
item.dc:creator: Ning Zhang, Arto Nurmikko

item.title: Deeply unrolled alternating projections for phase retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2610.17316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep unrolling methods for inverse problems augment traditional reconstruction algorithms with learned priors to improve their performance. These methods have been developed under the implicit assumption that the geometry of the measurement operator does not change between training and deployment; when this is no longer the case, the quality of obtained reconstructions can degrade significantly. In this paper, we argue that this is not an inherent limitation of the deep unrolling paradigm and can be mitigated by a careful choice of the underlying iterative algorithm. We propose a deep unrolling framework for the phase retrieval problem that augments the alternating projections method with a learned denoising step. Our method obtains high-quality reconstructions without the need for retraining in settings where conventional model-based alternatives struggle, such as when the dynamic range of the measurement operator changes significantly at test time.
item.dc:creator: Jiayi Yao, Vasileios Charisopoulos, Rebecca Willett

item.title: FedLoRD: Personalized Federated Learning based on Low-Rank Structures of Model Parameter Differences
item.description: arXiv:2610.17621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose FedLoRD, a personalized federated learning (PFL) method based on the low-rank structure of the differences between the global and personalized model parameters. PFL is a branch of federated learning that aims to learn models tailored to the local data of each client under biased local data distributions. In its local training, each client learns a personalized model by regularizing the difference between its model parameters and the global ones sent from the server. The regularization function needs to be designed with priors on the model parameter difference; however, the existing PFL methods rely on empirical choices (e.g., $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-norms), which do not take into account the actual characteristics of the difference. The resulting mismatch of priors can lead to suboptimal personalized models. To address this issue, we propose a PFL method whose regularizer is built on an observed characteristic of the model parameter differences: they are approximately low-rank at every layer. In our method, we first formulate a local training problem with nuclear norm regularization on the layer-wise differences. We further rewrite this problem via the factorized representation of the nuclear norm so that it can be efficiently solved by a plain stochastic gradient descent method. Image classification experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedLoRD outperforms several existing PFL methods.
item.dc:creator: Tsutahiro Fukuhara, Junya Hara, Hiroshi Higashi, Yuichi Tanaka

item.title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.17718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoliang Wang, Zhuo Chen, Chuanyang Zheng, Jiangwei Lao, Quanbin Wang, Honglin Lin, Jiajia Liu, Zhihong Lu, Hao Jin, Jian Wang, Lijun Wu

item.title: Provable Method of Moments for Cryo-EM
item.description: arXiv:2610.17892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional volume in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) from noisy tomographic projections acquired at unknown viewing rotations, drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. We show that, in a spherical-shell representation satisfying an explicit shell-separation condition, the first three moments generically determine the underlying real volume up to its intrinsic global $\mathrm{O}(3)$ ambiguity. The proof is constructive and yields a frequency-marching procedure that successively recovers the volume. Consequently, consistent recovery in the high-noise regime has sample complexity $n=\omega(\sigma^6)$, where $n$ is the number of observations and $\sigma^2$ is the noise variance. Numerical experiments validate the constructive recovery scheme under finite sampling and additive noise, and indicate that direct third-moment optimization can succeed beyond the structural assumptions required by the constructive proof.
item.dc:creator: Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory, Dan Edidin, Josh Katz, Shay Kreymer, Nir Sharon

item.title: Lifted Restricted Isometry Property and Fast Algorithm for Spectral Compressed Sensing With Near-Optimal Sample Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.18032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies the spectral compressed sensing problem, which aims to recover an $r$-spectrally-sparse signal of length $N$ from linear compressive measurements. We reformulate the problem as the recovery of a low-rank Hankel matrix. Motivated by this formulation, we propose a Lifted Restricted Isometry Property (LRIP) for the measurement matrix and show that Gaussian measurement matrices satisfy LRIP under certain conditions. Unlike classical RIP, LRIP imposes a rank constraint in the lifted matrix domain while taking measurements in the signal domain through the adjoint Hankel operator. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem efficiently, we introduce a Fast Iterative Hard Thresholding (FIHT) algorithm. Based on LRIP, we show that FIHT converges linearly to the true signal with high probability using $\mathcal{O}(r \ln r \ln^2 N)$ scaled Gaussian measurements, which is near-optimal up to log factors and improves the state-of-the-art order of $r^2$ for nonconvex Hankel methods. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the superiority of FIHT as compared to state-of-the-art convex methods in terms of phase transitions, computational time, and robustness to noise.
item.dc:creator: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang

item.title: Revisiting Error Feedback for Model Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2610.18139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study causal error-feedback coefficients as design variables for model quantization. Modeling instantaneous quantization errors as independent, zero-mean variables with a common fixed variance, we formulated a metric-dependent trace problem for designing feedback coefficients. The formulation resembles fixed-order GPTQ/LDLQ feedback and supports Jacobian-aware designs that account for downstream error propagation. For a positive-definite metric $\boldsymbol{H}$, we prove that the joint rotation-feedback trace minimum is $n\det(\boldsymbol{H})^{1/n}$ and present an attaining pair using the geometric mean decomposition. Experiments on synthetic networks, trained MLPs, and language models show benefits from downstream-sensitive feedback, but also reveal that trace optimality need not improve finite-level performance. Small QAT experiments further illustrate direct loss-driven feedback tuning with fixed or trainable network weights.
item.dc:creator: Wai-Yiu Keung, Chi Cui, Wing-Kin Ma, Jes\'us Cid-Sueiro, Hei Victor Cheng

item.title: FALLNEST: Dual-Domain Dataset Condensation of Imbalanced IMU Data for Wearable Fall Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.18260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wearable fall detection is hampered by rare fall events, scarce labeled IMU data, and the cost of training deep models on large, imbalanced corpora. Existing methods either rely on hand-crafted features with shallow classifiers, which limits learning from raw signals, or train deep networks on full datasets that require re-sampling to counter class skew and demand substantial data and compute. To address this, we propose a novel Fall detection framework via Normalized-gradient and Embedding matched Synthetic Time-frequency condensation, dubbed FALLNEST, a data-centric approach that distills large, imbalanced IMU datasets into tiny, class-balanced synthetic training sets. Building on dual-domain time-series condensation (CondTSC), FALLNEST introduces a fall-specific 7-channel input with accelerometer vector magnitude, class-balanced K-Means initialization, and normalized gradient matching with gradient clipping, combined with MMD-based embedding alignment and multi-view Fourier-domain augmentation, so that class balance arises from the condensed set itself rather than from re-sampling. We evaluate on SisFall, KFall, and MobiFall using strict subject-wise splits and naturally imbalanced test sets, reporting accuracy, Macro-F1, and PR-AUC over five seeds. A 102K-parameter TinyCNN trained on only 32 to 146 synthetic windows (about only 1% of the training windows) reaches 93.5-95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89-0.98 PR-AUC, with standard deviations of 1.0-1.7% in accuracy, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Rashi Niyas P, Ritika Jain, Hitika Tiwari

item.title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2610.18280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Simeunovi\'c, Baptiste Schubnel, Pierre-Jean Alet, Pascal Frossard, Rafael E. Carrillo

item.title: Application based Evaluation of an Efficient Spike-Encoder, "Spiketrum"
item.description: arXiv:2405.15927v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spike-based encoders represent information as sequences of spikes or pulses, which are transmitted between neurons. A prevailing consensus suggests that spike-based approaches demonstrate exceptional capabilities in capturing the temporal dynamics of neural activity and have the potential to provide energy-efficient solutions for low-power applications. The Spiketrum encoder efficiently compresses input data using spike trains or code sets (for non-spiking applications) and is adaptable to both hardware and software implementations, with lossless signal reconstruction capability. The paper proposes and assesses Spiketrum's hardware, evaluating its output under varying spike rates and its classification performance with popular spiking and non-spiking classifiers, and also assessing the quality of information compression and hardware resource utilization. The paper extensively benchmarks both Spiketrum hardware and its software counterpart against state-of-the-art, biologically-plausible encoders. The evaluations encompass benchmarking criteria, including classification accuracy, training speed, and sparsity when using encoder outputs in pattern recognition and classification with both spiking and non-spiking classifiers. Additionally, they consider encoded output entropy and hardware resource utilization and power consumption of the hardware version of the encoders. Results demonstrate Spiketrum's superiority in most benchmarking criteria, making it a promising choice for various applications. It efficiently utilizes hardware resources with low power consumption, achieving high classification accuracy. This work also emphasizes the potential of encoders in spike-based processing to improve the efficiency and performance of neural computing systems.
item.dc:creator: MHD Anas Alsakkal, Runze Wang, Jayawan Wijekoon, Huajin Tang

item.title: A General-Purpose Neuromorphic Sensor based on Spiketrum Algorithm: Hardware Details and Real-life Applications
item.description: arXiv:2501.18799v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically inspired computational paradigm, enabling energy-efficient data processing through spike-based information transmission. Despite notable advancements in hardware for SNNs, spike encoding has largely remained software-dependent, limiting efficiency. This paper addresses the need for adaptable and resource-efficient spike encoding hardware by presenting an area-optimized hardware implementation of the Spiketrum algorithm, which encodes time-varying analogue signals into spatiotemporal spike patterns. Unlike earlier performance-optimized designs, which prioritize speed, our approach focuses on reducing hardware footprint, achieving a 52% reduction in Block RAMs (BRAMs), 31% fewer Digital Signal Processing (DSP) slices, and a 6% decrease in Look-Up Tables (LUTs). The proposed implementation has been verified on an FPGA and successfully integrated into an IC using TSMC180 technology. Experimental results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in real-world applications, including sound and ECG classification. This work highlights the trade-offs between performance and resource efficiency, offering a flexible, scalable solution for neuromorphic systems in power-sensitive applications like cochlear implants and neural devices.
item.dc:creator: MHD Anas Alsakkal, Runze Wang, Piotr Dudek, Jayawan Wijekoon

item.title: Markovian Continuity of the MMSE
item.description: arXiv:2504.14659v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimation is widely used in signal processing, information theory, and related fields. Despite its practical robustness, the MMSE can be discontinuous under standard notions of stochastic convergence. To bridge this gap, we review classical counterexamples to the continuity of the MMSE and identify two obstructions: failure of second-moment convergence and approximating observations carrying more information about the limit estimand than the limit observation does. Motivated by practical acquisition mechanisms, we study MMSE continuity under two natural constraints: (1) continuity of the second moment, and (2) a degradedness (Markov) restriction ensuring that each approximating observation is no more informative than the limit observation is about the limit estimand. Under these conditions, we establish continuity of the MMSE and of the MMSE estimator. We provide complementary semicontinuity results and continuity guarantees in related settings and establish continuity under linear estimation. We further extend the analysis to the families of Bregman divergences and continuous metric and generalized metric cost functions, including the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Elad Domanovitz, Anatoly Khina

item.title: Sparse Signal Reconstruction for Track-Before-Detect
item.description: arXiv:2506.18177v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurately tracking an unknown and time-varying number of objects in complex environments is a challenging problem in radar and sonar sensing. The track-before-detect (TkBD) paradigm aims to avoid a detection stage by operating directly on sensor data to prevent information loss. This paper introduces a novel TkBD method based on a superpositional signal model adopted from the sparse signal reconstruction literature. The resulting TkBD measurement model accounts for sensor data correlations, amplitude fluctuations, and unknown measurement noise variance. By retaining relative phase information in complex-valued sensor data, the proposed measurement model supports phase-coherent processing directly within the TkBD method. It also enables the accurate representation of the physics of the data-generating process in the statistical model used for TkBD, including the complex acoustic wavefields used in matched-field processing. To accommodate measurements from multiple sensors or frequencies, we introduce a general multi-snapshot, multi-dictionary formulation of this model. The proposed statistical model is suitable for a wide range of problems in active and passive radar, active and passive sonar, as well as integrated sensing and communication systems. Based on a factor graph representation of the proposed model, a scalable belief propagation (BP) method is developed to perform efficient Bayesian inference. Experimental results obtained with both synthetic radar data and real acoustic data for matched-field processing demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art conventional multiobject tracking (MOT) methods.
item.dc:creator: Mingchao Liang, Florian Meyer

item.title: Dual-Waveguide Pinching Antennas for PLS: Parallel Placement or Orthogonal Placement?
item.description: arXiv:2510.11044v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pinching antennas (PAs) represent an emerging flexible-antenna paradigm, where movable PAs arranged along dielectric waveguides enable on-demand customization of wireless channel characteristics. This paper exploits PAs to enhance physical-layer security (PLS) by increasing the channel diversity gap between legitimate users (LUs) and eavesdroppers (Eves). We concentrate on a dual-waveguide PA system, in which each waveguide is equipped with multiple PAs to serve multiple LUs under wiretapping from an Eve. Two waveguide placement schemes are studied: parallel placement and orthogonal placement. To capture practical waveguide propagation effects, we adopt two in-waveguide channel models: in-waveguide phase shifts, and in-waveguide phase shifts and attenuation. We formulate secure sum rate (SSR) and secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problems, and develop a two-stage optimization framework to tackle these non-convex problems. In the first stage, we design a feasibility-enhanced particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm named FeaPSO to search for valid PA positions complying with minimum inter-PA spacing constraints. The second stage leverages successive convex approximation (SCA) to jointly optimize baseband beamforming and artificial noise vectors. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed two-stage algorithm and confirm that PA adjustment yields substantial gains in both SSR and SEE. Moreover, the simulation outcomes demonstrate the performance benefits brought by orthogonal waveguide placement for PLS enhancement.
item.dc:creator: Yang Lu, Xinke Xie, Yanqing Xu, Bo Ai, Octavia A. Dobre, Arumugam Nallanathan

item.title: Short Blocks, Fast Sensing: Finite Blocklength Tradeoffs in RIS-Assisted ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2511.02673v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a cornerstone for future sixth-generation (6G) networks, enabling simultaneous connectivity and environmental awareness. However, practical realization faces significant challenges, including residual self-interference (SI) in full-duplex (FD) systems and performance degradation of short-packet transmissions under finite blocklength (FBL) constraints. This work studies a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted FD ISAC system serving multiple downlink users while tracking a moving target, explicitly accounting for SI and FBL effects in both communication and sensing. We formulate an optimization framework to minimize service adaptation gaps while ensuring sensing reliability, solved via alternating optimization and successive convex approximation. Numerical results show that short blocklengths enable fast adaptation but increase radar outage due to fewer pulses and motion sensitivity, whereas longer blocklengths improve SINR and reduce outages but allow target motion to degrade sensing. A regime-dependent "sweet spot" emerges, where blocklength and beamformer allocation jointly balance throughput and sensing, with HD favored at very short blocklengths and FD at longer blocklengths. RIS-assisted optimization expands the FD-operating regime, enabling reliable communication and radar sensing at lower blocklengths.
item.dc:creator: Adam Umra, Kevin Weinberger, Aymen Khaleel, Gerald Enzner, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Interpretable Multimodal EEG-ECG Framework for Neonatal Seizure Prediction and Patient-Adaptive Transfer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2511.14110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neonatal seizures carry substantial risks of acute brain injury and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment, motivating the need for timely identification of impending seizure activity. While continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) monitoring remains the clinical gold standard, reliable patient-independent seizure prediction in neonates remains largely under-explored. We propose an interpretable multimodal framework that combines EEG and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals for neonatal seizure prediction. Our method uses mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) representations processed by a lightweight (approx. 70k-parameter) convolutional neural network with squeeze-and-excitation attention. The framework was evaluated on the Helsinki neonatal EEG-ECG dataset and the Siena scalp EEG-ECG dataset. Under strict leave-one-patient-out (LOPO) evaluation, patient-independent prediction proved challenging (mean accuracy 58.5%, F1-score 60.3%), highlighting substantial inter-subject variability in neonatal EEG. However, fine-tuning the pretrained model with only five minutes of patient-specific data per class improved performance to 95.87% accuracy and 95.85% F1-score, demonstrating the feasibility of rapid patient-adaptive transfer learning. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified informative EEG channels that showed partial spatial agreement with clinically reported seizure origins. These findings suggest that fully patient-independent neonatal seizure prediction remains challenging, but that patient-adaptive fine-tuning with a small amount of data may provide a practical pathway toward personalized neonatal seizure prediction systems.
item.dc:creator: Sithmini Ranasingha, Agasthi Haputhanthri, Hansa Marasinghe, Kithmin Wickremasinghe, Nima Wickramasinghe, Jithangi Wanigasinghe, Chamira U. S. Edussooriya, Joshua P. Kulasingham

item.title: On the Impact of Channel Aging and Doppler-Affected Clutter on OFDM ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2601.05032v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The temporal evolution of the propagation environment plays a central role in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. A slow-time evolution manifests as channel aging in communication links, while a fast-time one is associated with non-zero Doppler clutter. Nevertheless, the joint impact of these two phenomena on ISAC performance has been largely overlooked. This paper addresses this research gap in a network utilizing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing waveforms. Here, a base station simultaneously serves a user equipment (UE) device and performs monostatic sensing. Channel aging is captured through an autoregressive model with exponential correlation decay. Clutter is modeled as a collection of uncorrelated, coherent patches with non-zero Doppler, resulting in a Kronecker-separable covariance structure. We propose an aging-aware channel estimator that uses prior pilot observations to estimate the time-varying UE channel, characterized by a non-isotropic multipath fading structure. The clutter's structure enables a novel low-complexity pre-detection radar processing pipeline: clutter statistics are estimated from raw data and subsequently used to suppress the clutter's action, after which range-angle and range-velocity maps are computed. We evaluate the influence of frame length and pilot history on channel estimation accuracy and demonstrate substantial performance gains over block fading in low-to-moderate mobility regimes. The sensing pipeline is implemented in a clutter-dominated environment, demonstrating that effective clutter suppression can be achieved under practical configurations. We analyze the robustness of our proposed pipeline against non-separable clutter by introducing a controllable degree of non-separability. Our results highlight the benefit of sensing streams and that our pipeline can withstand a moderate degree of non-separability.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rivetti, Gabor Fodor, Emil Bj\"ornson, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Convexity Meets Curvature: Lifted Near-Field Super-Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2602.14063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extra-large apertures, high carrier frequencies, and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) are pushing array processing into the Fresnel region, where spherical wavefronts induce a range-dependent phase across the aperture. This curvature breaks the Fourier/Vandermonde structure behind classical subspace methods, and it is especially limiting with hybrid front-ends that provide only a small number of pilot measurements. Consequently, practical systems need continuous angle resolution and joint angle-range inference where many near-field approaches still rely on costly 2D gridding. We show that convexity can meet curvature via a lifted, gridless superresolution framework for near-field measurements. The key is a Bessel-Vandermonde factorization of the Fresnel-phase manifold that exposes a hidden Vandermonde structure in angle while isolating the range dependence into a compact coefficient map. Building on this, we introduce a lifting that maps each range bin and continuous angle to a structured rank-one atom, converting the nonlinear near-field model into a linear inverse problem over a row-sparse matrix. Recovery is posed as atomic-norm minimization and an explicit dual characterization via bounded trigonometric polynomials yields certificate-based localization that super-resolves off-grid angles and identifies active range bins. Simulations with strongly undersampled hybrid observations validate reliable joint angle-range recovery for next-generation wireless and ISAC systems.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Daei, G\'abor Fodor, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Combining scEEG and PPG for reliable sleep staging
item.description: arXiv:2602.15042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable sleep staging remains challenging for lightweight wearable devices such as single-channel electroencephalography (scEEG) or photoplethysmography (PPG). scEEG offers direct measurement of cortical activity and serves as the foundation for sleep staging, yet exhibits limited performance on light sleep stages. PPG provides a low-cost complement that captures autonomic signatures effective for detecting light sleep. However, prior PPG-based methods rely on full night recordings (8 - 10 hours) as input context, which is less practical to provide timely feedback for sleep intervention. In this work, we investigate scEEG-PPG fusion for 4-class sleep staging under short-window (30 s - 30 min) constraints. First, we evaluate the temporal context required for each modality, to better understand the relationship of sleep staging performance with respect to monitoring window. Second, we investigate three fusion strategies: score-level fusion, cross-attention fusion enabling feature-level interactions, and Mamba-enhanced fusion incorporating temporal context modeling. Third, we train and evaluate on the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) dataset and perform cross-dataset validation on the Cleveland Family Study (CFS) and the Apnea, Bariatric surgery, and CPAP (ABC) datasets. The Mamba-enhanced fusion achieves the best performance on MESA (Cohen's Kappa $\kappa$ = 0.798, Acc = 86.9%), with particularly notable improvement in light sleep classification (F1-score: 85.63% vs. 77.76%, recall: 82.85% vs. 69.95% for scEEG alone), and generalizes well to CFS and ABC datasets with different populations. These findings suggest that scEEG-PPG fusion is a promising approach for lightweight wearable based sleep monitoring, offering a pathway toward more accessible sleep health assessment. Source code of this project can be found at: https://github.com/DavyWJW/scEEG-PPGFusion
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Wang, Liang Xu, Shuntian Zheng, Yu Guan, Kaichen Wang, Ziqing Zhang, Chen Chen, Laurence T. Yang, Sai Gu, M. Jamal Deen

item.title: Joint Communication and Sensing Security in MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems via Artificial Noise and Ghosts
item.description: arXiv:2602.20045v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables efficient sharing of wireless resources to support emerging applications, but it also introduces new sensing-based security vulnerabilities. Here, potential communication security threats include confidential messages intended for legitimate users being intercepted, and unauthorized receivers (Eves) passively exploiting target echoes to infer sensing parameters without users being aware. Despite these risks, the joint protection of sensing and communication security in ISAC systems remains unexplored. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dual-secure ISAC framework that simultaneously protects sensing and communication against passive sensing Eves and communication Eves, without requiring their channel state information (CSI). Specifically, transmit beamformers are jointly designed to inject artificial noise (AN) to introduce interference to communication Eves, while deliberately distorting the reference signal available to sensing Eves to impair their sensing capability. Furthermore, the proposed design generates artificial ghosts (AGs) with fake angle-delay-Doppler profiles. The legitimate sensing receiver can suppress these AGs using its prior knowledge of the true target directions, whereas sensing Eves cannot, thereby significantly reducing their probability of correctly detecting the true targets. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively enhances both communication and sensing security, while preserving the performance of communication users and legitimate sensing receivers.
item.dc:creator: Yinchao Yang, Prabhat Raj Gautam, Yathreb Bouazizi, Mohammad Kazemi, Michael Breza, Julie A. McCann

item.title: Joint and Streamwise Distributed MIMO Satellite Communications with Multi-Antenna Ground Users
item.description: arXiv:2603.12914v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a low Earth orbit downlink communication, where multiple satellites jointly serve multi-antenna ground users, transmitting multiple spatial streams per user. Using a line-of-sight-dominant satellite channel model with statistical channel state information, including angular information and large-scale fading, we study two distributed transmission modes with different fronthaul requirements. First, for joint transmission, where all satellites transmit all user streams, we formulate a sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem under general convex power constraints and address the intractability of the exact ergodic SE expression by adopting a tractable approximation. Exploiting the equivalence between sum SE maximization and weighted sum mean square error minimization, we derive a novel iterative transceiver design. Second, to reduce fronthaul load, we propose streamwise transmission, where each stream is sent by a single satellite, and develop an eigenmode-based stream-satellite association using participation factors and a maximum-weight bipartite matching problem solved by the Hungarian algorithm. Numerical simulations evaluate the validity of the SE approximation, demonstrate conditions under which streamwise transmission performs nearly optimally or trades SE for lower overhead, highlight the impact of stream/user loading, and show substantial performance gains over conventional benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Ramezani, Emil Bj\"ornson

item.title: A Ray-Based Characterization of Satellite-to-Urban Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2603.25621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The evolution toward 6G communication systems is expected to rely on integrated three-dimensional network architectures where terrestrial infrastructures coexist with non-terrestrial stations such as satellites, enabling ubiquitous connectivity and service continuity. In this context, accurate channel models for satellite-to-ground propagation in urban environments are essential, particularly for user equipment located at street level where obstruction and multipath effects are significant. This work investigates satellite-to-urban propagation through deterministic ray-tracing simulations. Three representative urban layouts are considered, namely dense urban, urban, and suburban. Multiple use cases are investigated, including handheld devices, vehicular terminals, and fixed rooftop receivers operating across several frequency bands. The analysis focuses on the relative importance of competing propagation mechanisms and on four key channel parameters, namely shadowing standard deviation, Rician \(K\)-factor, delay spread and Doppler spread, which are relevant for the calibration of channel models to be used in link- and system-level simulations. Results show that elevation and receiver placement strongly shape fading and dispersion, antenna directivity affects shadowing differently under LoS and NLoS conditions, urban morphology produces nontrivial multipath trends, and terminal mobility largely governs Doppler spread.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\`o Cenni, Marina Barbiroli, Vittorio Degli-Esposti, Enrico M. Vitucci, Carla Amatetti, Franco Fuschini

item.title: Near-Field Integrated Sensing and Communication with a Uniform Circular Array
item.description: arXiv:2604.08160v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Near-field (NF) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is studied for a uniform circular array (UCA) and monostatic sensing. A continuous-time channel model is derived for the spherical wavefront and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing. A multi-slot Cram\`er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for joint range-angle-Doppler estimation is derived under a slow-motion approximation, showing how the signal delay and wavefront curvature affect the range bound. A transmit beamformer that minimizes the position CRLB is designed via gradient descent, and a maximum-likelihood estimator is obtained by using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm initialized with a grid search. Simulations show that increasing the UCA radius improves angle and motion estimation at all distances, but improves the range bound only at distances far inside the Rayleigh distance, and lowers the reliable communication rate.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Zaniboni, Mark F. Flanagan, Gerhard Kramer

item.title: Living Off the Grid: Continuous Range-Angle Super-Resolution for Near-Field XL-MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2604.10234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Near-field extremely large multiple input multiple output (XL-MIMO) breaks the assumptions that make classical super-resolution effective: the receiver acquires only a limited set of compressed pilot observations, while each propagation path is jointly determined by angle and distance under a spherical-wave model. This invalidates the far-field Vandermonde structure exploited by conventional methods, and many existing near-field formulations remain only gridless by discretizing range and angle and thus inheriting mismatch, coherence, and resolution loss. This paper develops a continuous 2D super-resolution framework for hybrid near-field measurements that avoids range and angle gridding. The key idea is to reparameterize distance through inverse range, which reveals a compact spectral structure for the near-field spherical-wave manifold. Building on this observation, we introduce a panelized weighted fitting strategy that converts the range-dependent Fresnel terms into a stable transform-domain representation, resulting in a lifted mode, in which each continuous range-angle pair is embedded as a structured rank-one atom and the measurement model remains linear under hybrid combining. Recovery is then posed as a 2D atomic norm minimization, with path localization certified through a dual polynomial over the transformed domain. Numerical experiments show exact support recovery in the noiseless setting using only few compressed hybrid measurements. These results establish the proposed inverse-range atomic norm viewpoint as a new gridless foundation for near-field sensing and channel estimation in hybrid XL-MIMO and integrated sensing and communication systems.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Daei, Gabor Fodor, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Cramer-Rao Bound Analysis of Bistatic ISAC Under Partial Symbol Knowledge and Clutter
item.description: arXiv:2604.11426v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems rely on communication waveforms to perform sensing tasks, thus making their sensing performance strongly dependent on the level of communication symbol knowledge available to the sensing receivers. However, the existing literature fails to capture this dependency, often relying on assumptions of full symbol knowledge. In this paper, we present a Cramer Rao bound (CRB) analysis of a bistatic ISAC network with heterogeneous uplink and downlink illumination and structured clutter. We consider different symbol knowledge regimes by modeling unknown communication symbols as nuisance parameters. Assuming a temporal evolution of the communication channel, we derive a correlation aware channel estimator and an expression for the UEs uplink spectral efficiency. Numerical results show the CRB degradation induced by clutter and symbol uncertainty and how this can affect resource allocation policies. We also show the performance gain of our channel estimator over conventional block fading architectures.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rivetti, Gabor Fodor, Emil Bjornson, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: SSB-Based Sensing-Assisted Robust Beamforming for High-Mobility UAV Communications in LAWN
item.description: arXiv:2604.19010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-mobility uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communications in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWN) demand reliable beamforming, while conventional feedback-based schemes suffer from excessive overhead and severe misalignment under rapid trajectory variations. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an SSB-based sensing-assisted predictive robust beamforming framework that replaces explicit CSI feedback with sensing-driven state estimation and uncertainty-aware optimization. Leveraging the periodic 'always-on' synchronization signal block (SSB), a hierarchical sensing algorithm tailored for hybrid digital-analog uniform planar arrays is developed, combining 2D range-velocity profiling and augmented beamspace multiple signal classification (MUSIC). By integrating a locally-focused analog receive beamformer, the proposed sensing design can ensure energy accumulates across different radio-frequency (RF) chains while resolving angular ambiguity. An extended Kalman filter (EKF) is further employed to track UAV states between sparse synchronization-signal (SS) bursts, and a covariance correction is introduced to characterize maneuver-induced prediction uncertainties. Based on the derived statistical distributions of range and angular parameters, the communication channel is modeled through predictive correlation matrices rather than instantaneous CSI, leading to a multi-user robust beamforming formulation that maximizes average network sum-rate under uncertainty. The resulting nonconvex problem is efficiently solved via successive convex approximation and alternating minimization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances spectral efficiency and link stability compared with feedback-based beamforming and non-robust beamforming design, particularly in high-mobility and large-SSB-interval scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Aimin Tang, Shuhan Wang, Chongrui Wang, Yin Xu

item.title: A Survey on the Symbiosis of Artificial Intelligence and Terahertz Networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.22706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Terahertz (THz) band (0.1-10 THz) has emerged as a critical frontier for future communication systems, offering ultra-wide bandwidths that enable Terabits-per-second (Tbps) wireless links and high-precision sensing and imaging. However, practical deployment of THz systems is hindered by unique challenges, including intricate channel characteristics, high-dimensional and large-scale optimization problems, and highly dynamic network environments. Artificial Intelligence (AI) serves as a transformative enabler to address these challenges, providing robust capabilities for precise modeling, advanced signal processing, complex optimization, real-time decision-making, and prediction, among others. Reciprocally, the unprecedented bandwidth and high-resolution sensing capabilities of THz networks provide a promising physical infrastructure for AI, facilitating training, inference, and data collection. This survey presents a systematic and comprehensive overview of AI-driven solutions across the entire THz communication network and the symbiosis of AI and THz networks. To begin with, a foundational overview of AI technologies tailored for wireless communications is presented. Subsequently, AI-based innovations are investigated, spanning from hardware design, channel modeling, physical layer optimization, up to higher-layer network protocols and advanced THz services, including mobile edge computing and sensing-empowered applications. In parallel, the capacity of THz networks to serve AI is examined, underscoring a profound paradigm shift towards a mutual symbiosis where AI and THz co-evolve and empower each other. Finally, by synthesizing these state-of-the-art advancements and identifying open research directions, this survey highlights the potential of AI in copilot with development of THz communication systems.
item.dc:creator: Chong Han, Jingting Jiang, Meixia Tao, Wenjun Zhang

item.title: Phase-Time Array Enabled Multistatic Sensing with Multi-Level Fusion for UAV Localization
item.description: arXiv:2605.04919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multistatic collaborative sensing, existing parameter-level fusion methods suffer from severe error amplification in geometrically unfavorable regions. Conventional receiver architectures present an additional challenge: analog phased arrays incur substantial beam sweeping overhead, while fully digital arrays demand prohibitive hardware costs. This paper proposes a multistatic sensing framework based on a phase-time array (PTA), whose rainbow beamforming maps spatial directions to OFDM subcarriers, achieving wide-angle coverage with a single RF chain and a favorable accuracy-complexity trade-off relative to both phased array and fully digital receivers. To suppress geometry-induced error hotspots, two parameter-level fusion schemes are developed: a GDOP-weighted analytical estimator (GDOP-WLS) and a lightweight multilayer perceptron (PF-MLP). An end-to-end signal-level convolutional neural network (SF-CNN) is further designed to directly regress target coordinates from raw received signals, bypassing cascaded parameter estimation. Simulation results show that the parameter-level schemes effectively mitigate localized error amplification with minimal computational overhead, while SF-CNN attains sub-meter positioning accuracy, at the cost of higher model complexity that can be offset by GPU acceleration. Power-matched training further extends both schemes' accuracy across a wide power range.
item.dc:creator: Ming Gao, Jianhua Mo, Meixia Tao

item.title: Map2APS: A Physically Grounded Benchmark for Direct Angle Power Spectrum Prediction from Urban Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2605.14989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Angle power spectrum (APS) characterizes the directional distribution of received signal power and is directly relevant to beam management and MIMO processing. While environment-aware learning has been widely studied for radio maps and path loss, direct map-to-APS prediction still lacks a standardized large-scale benchmark. This paper presents Map2APS, a physically grounded benchmark constructed from intelligent ray-tracing (IRT) path-level propagation records.
